claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation. Let me start with a few basic questions:

1. **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex who is 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (or more) towards his upkeep, such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. A few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex has been in hospital for a while now - about 3 months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for letting me know. This is important information as it may affect your eligibility.

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?** (For example, buying him things he needs, treats, clothes, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I haven't been able to afford to spend money on his needs while he's in there, unfortunately.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, thank you for being honest about your situation. Let me ask one final question:

**Has Alex been in hospital continuously for these 3 months, or has he had any breaks where he came home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital continuously for the whole time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

Here's why:

While you meet the basic eligibility requirements (you live in the UK, you have parental responsibility for Alex, he normally lives with you, and no one else is claiming), there's a specific rule about children in hospital that affects your eligibility.

When a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks continuously, Child Benefit entitlement usually ends. Alex has been in hospital for 3 months (12 weeks), which reaches this threshold. There is an exception to this rule - you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on your child while they're in hospital. However, since you've mentioned that you haven't been able to afford to spend money on Alex's needs while he's been in hospital, this exception doesn't apply to your situation.

I understand this may be difficult news, especially during what must already be a challenging time with Alex in hospital. If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex comes home or if you're able to regularly spend money on his needs), your eligibility may be reassessed.

After the 12-week limit, the claimant is usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit. There is an exception if the claimant regularly spends money on the child while they are in hospital, but the claimant has confirmed they have not been able to afford to spend money on Alex's needs while he's been in hospital. Therefore, as Alex has been in hospital for 12 weeks continuously and the claimant is not regularly spending money on him, the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
